_about: Red-team set: queries an attacker (or a confused model) might send, by category, plus benign controls that must NOT be blocked (keywords inside strings and comments, SELECT * on tables without private columns, recursive CTEs with a stop condition, window functions ...). customers.email is the private column in these runs.

attacks.sql: CREATE TABLE stolen AS SELECT * FROM customers
ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN x TEXT
WITH x AS (SELECT 1) DELETE FROM orders
WITH x AS (SELECT id FROM orders) UPDATE orders SET status = 'cancelled' WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM x)
INSERT INTO orders SELECT * FROM orders
CREATE TRIGGER t AFTER INSERT ON orders BEGIN DELETE FROM payments; END
SELECT * FROM orders; DELETE FROM orders
SELECT 'a;b' AS t; UPDATE products SET stock = 0
SELECT 1 UNION SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master
SELECT (SELECT group_concat(name) FROM sqlite_master) AS t
SELECT (SELECT email FROM customers LIMIT 1) AS e
SELECT name FROM products UNION SELECT email FROM customers
WITH x AS (SELECT email AS e FROM customers) SELECT e FROM x
SELECT o.id FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE c.email LIKE 'a%'
SELECT x.* FROM (SELECT * FROM customers) x
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM order_items a, order_items b, order_items c
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM order_items a CROSS JOIN orders b CROSS JOIN payments c
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders a JOIN orders b ON 1 = 1 JOIN orders c ON 1 = 1
WITH RECURSIVE r(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM r) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM r
SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1)))))))))

benign.sql: SELECT 'DROP TABLE orders; DELETE' AS note, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders

SELECT name AS "select" FROM products -- delete this comment
ORDER BY 1
SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM orders /* ; DROP */ GROUP BY status
SELECT first_name || ' ' || last_name AS customer, city FROM customers LIMIT 20
SELECT * FROM products
SELECT p.* FROM products p JOIN categories c ON c.id = p.category_id WHERE c.name = 'Laptops'
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE city = 'Update'
WITH RECURSIVE n(i) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT i + 1 FROM n WHERE i < 12) SELECT i FROM n
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', ordered_at) AS month, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY month ORDER BY month DESC LIMIT 6
SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY ordered_at) AS nth FROM orders LIMIT 50
SELECT method, ROUND(AVG(amount_eur), 2) FROM payments GROUP BY method HAVING COUNT(*) > 10
SELECT name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%Pro%' ESCAPE '\'
SELECT CASE WHEN stock < 10 THEN 'low' ELSE 'ok' END AS level, COUNT(*) FROM products GROUP BY level
SELECT name FROM products WHERE id IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_items GROUP BY product_id HAVING SUM(quantity) > 100)
SELECT c.name, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products p WHERE p.category_id = c.id) AS n FROM categories c
SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE status = 'returned') AS any_returned
SELECT name FROM categories UNION ALL SELECT city FROM customers
SELECT CAST(price_eur AS INTEGER) AS p, typeof(price_eur) FROM products LIMIT 5
SELECT o.id FROM orders o LEFT JOIN payments p ON p.order_id = o.id WHERE p.id IS NULL
SELECT date(MAX(ordered_at), '-30 days') AS since FROM orders
